SMTO-CTX-0025 — SMTO couldn't carry this task into a new conversation

GUID: d5145944-8fac-42ba-87a6-af4e8c08001c
Slug: task-context-snapshot-limit
Domain: CTX · Subsystem: ctx

What happened

  • Continue in new conversation packs a short summary of this task to bring along. Even after shortening, the summary was too big to fit, so the new conversation wasn't created. The original task is unchanged.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Start a new conversation and write a short description of what the earlier task did and what you need next. A description you write yourself doesn't go through the automatic summary, so its size limit doesn't apply.
  2. In the new conversation, select Add context, choose Add files to conversation, and attach only the files the next task really needs. Every attached file made the automatic summary bigger, so bringing only the needed ones keeps the new task small.
  3. If you need the earlier task's results, open the original conversation and copy the important parts into your new message. The original task and its results are still there and unchanged.

What success looks like

  • A new conversation opens and its first task can see the description and files you brought over.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't delete the original conversation; it still holds the full task and its results.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The task-fork snapshot builder could not shrink the task summary under its character limit (21,600 before results, 24,000 total) after excerpting the request and results, because the remaining fixed fields (attachment entries, Task Contract, IDs) alone are too large.

What this means

  • The task-fork builder cannot fit its bounded snapshot after its permitted excerpts and evidence selection; this is a snapshot-container limit, not a model context measurement. Context admission, storage and reading are separate from executing a tool mutation. Preserve existing task state and receipts; a context diagnostic does not authorize replay of earlier operations.

Why this can happen

  • The task-fork builder cannot fit its bounded snapshot after its permitted excerpts and evidence selection; this is a snapshot-container limit, not a model context measurement.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the selected attachment metadata and contract size alongside the snapshot limit; reducing model output tokens does not change this container limit.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the source task in build_snapshot (task_fork_context.py): once original_request, result_summary and final_result are excerpted below 100 characters, the remaining fields (attachment metadata, the task_contract copy, IDs and JSON escaping) still exceed MAX_CONTEXT_CHARS - 2400 or MAX_CONTEXT_CHARS (24,000). Start a new conversation manually with the needed files; do not raise the limit or bypass the scope checks to force the fork through.
  • Reduce the selected continuation scope or attachments while preserving the original task and evidence.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • A supported fork produces a bounded snapshot with explicit omitted-item counts and links to retained evidence.

What not to do

  • Do not bypass scope or ownership checks to force a larger operation through.

Technical notes

  • Context admission, storage and reading are separate from executing a tool mutation. Preserve existing task state and receipts; a context diagnostic does not authorize replay of earlier operations.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
